root.name: Hungarian Opening: Reversed Brooklyn Defense, Brooklyn Benko Gambit
root.moves: 1. g3 e5 2. Nf3 e4 3. Ng1 Nf6 4. b4

overview: Reversed Alekhine move order: 1.g3 e5 2.Nf3 e4 3.Ng1 Nf6 4.b4 is White's attempt at a Benko-style pawn offer, where ...Bxb4 gives Black a pawn for little. Black has space and a pawn on e4, and White has lost time with the knight going back to g1. Unsure of the practical theory; the position is a rare irregular line.

white_ideas.idea: Offer the b-pawn to open lines for Bb2 and the a1-rook
Use the fianchetto bishop on the long diagonal against e5/e4

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4 and keep the pawn, with the e4 space gain
Develop smoothly and undermine the e4 pawn's support with ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Black pawn on e4 cramps White; White fianchetto on g2 and b2 against a centre of e4/d5

character.notes: Pawn offer on move 4 with Black ahead in space; unbalanced but quiet.

gambit.notes: 4.b4 Bxb4 wins a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.notes: Strong players would consider 4.b4 close to unsound; White's compensation is thin after the knight retreat.

structure.notes: e4 pawn cramps White, centre not locked; queenside lines may open after ...Bxb4.

approach.notes: Irregular first move and a rare gambit; seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Hard to justify; a gambit line that is not a good repertoire choice.

character.reason: A pawn offer with Black ahead in space leads to unbalanced play.

gambit.reason: b4 is a pawn Black can take and keep.

soundness.reason: The pawn offer has little compensation after the knight retreat.

structure.reason: Centre not yet decided, with Black's e4 pawn the only fixed element.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner, little theory so not Advanced.

plans.reason: Bb2 and g2 fianchettos with queenside pawn play.
